correctness.rationale: The order-p-line partition is exhaustive and disjoint. Each line block is a clique, distinct blocks are anticomplete, and the pure q-clique is adjacent to all mixed generators. These facts give sharp lower and upper bounds for ordinary and total domination. In any perfect matching, an edge can involve selected vertices from at most one line block, forcing at least t matching edges; two mixed generators in each block attain 2t.

evidence: Doostabadi--Farrokhi prove that p-group proper-power components correspond to minimal cyclic subgroups and analyze nilpotent connectivity, but do not give the present two-prime block domination formulas.
Bera--Dey--Patra--Sahoo relate ordinary domination to prime-order subgroups and determine ordinary values for broad nilpotent classes; their article does not treat total or paired domination.
Haynes--Slater define paired domination for general graphs and establish its relation to ordinary and total domination, without algebraic power graphs.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The strongest same-object connectivity source, the strongest same-object ordinary-domination source, and the foundational strengthened-domination source were compared at statement level.

evidence: The 2014 p-group component theorem does not apply directly to G because G has two distinct prime divisors; its nilpotent theorem gives connectivity/diameter rather than the line-block matching structure.
The 2025 ordinary value controls only the minimum size of a dominating set. It gives no selected-neighbor condition and no perfect-matching lower bound.
The new paired proof needs the fact that distinct order-p line blocks are anticomplete and that a matching edge can account for at most one required block.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The total and paired formulas require adjacency inside the chosen set and a blockwise matching count; neither follows formally from the published ordinary domination number or connectivity statements.

Neither inspected source states total or paired domination for the elementary-abelian-by-cyclic prime family, and the paired matching obstruction is not implied by the ordinary parameter.
